title: Process Isolation vs Thread Shared Memory Scenario

candidate.statement: An HTTP server handles concurrent requests. Analyze the difference when worker units are spawned as processes versus threads: if Worker A mutates a global in-memory cache pointer, does Worker B observe this mutation under multi-processing vs multi-threading?
constraints: Operating System: POSIX / Linux virtual memory architecture

examples.observation: Visible to Worker B only in multi-threaded model

hints: Consider virtual address spaces, page tables, and whether memory is isolated or shared.
short_diagnostics: Why does multi-processing require explicit IPC (pipes/shared memory) to share state?

evaluator.reference_solution: Under multi-processing, each process has its own isolated virtual address space and private page tables. Worker A mutating memory does not affect Worker B without explicit shared memory IPC. Under multi-threading, threads share the same virtual address space and process heap; Worker A mutation is immediately visible in Worker B address space.
evaluator.rubric: Candidate clearly articulates isolated virtual address spaces for processes vs shared heap/address space for threads.
known_pitfalls: Confusing thread stack isolation with process heap sharing.
evaluator.oracle_notes: Crucial foundation before diagnosing race conditions.
